html:
Kunjen is the map's name for the Uw Oykangand, Olkola and related Aboriginal Australian peoples of inland Cape York Peninsula, who speak the Kunjen language, also called Uw. Their country lies along the upper Mitchell and Alice rivers.

Kunjen is a Paman language, part of the large Pama-Nyungan family, and it is close to the speech of the Thaayorre on the Gulf coast. Their neighbours included the Kokomini and the Koko Bera.

Cattle stations took much of their country in the late 1800s. Many Kunjen people came to live at the Mitchell River mission, founded in 1916 near the river mouth and now the town of Kowanyama.
